Prime Members, it's time! Amazon's Black Friday sale has officially commenced. Starting a full ten days before today, Black Friday, November 27, the sale will wrap up on Cyber Monday, November 30.

Amazon's Black Friday sale has deep discounts across a wide range of products, including Amazon's own devices such as Kindle e-readers, Fire TV sticks and Echo smart devices. There are also bargains on home and kitchen appliances, the latest tech, fashion, beauty, lifestyle and fitness, electronics and so much more.

Some hot Amazon deals I'm adding to my cart this Black Friday include 47% off the Kindle Colorsoft and 62% off a Nespresso Vertuo Pop bundle.

While Amazon's Black Friday sale is open to all shoppers, Prime members can expect exclusive member-only deals, free delivery, and access to all of Amazon Prime's benefits. Not a Prime Member? Sign up for a 30-day free trial here.

The Blink Mini 2K+ is an affordable indoor camera with a wired connection that offers high-resolution live-view footage, a built-in LED spotlight and two-way audio. The camera also detects motion, so you can put your mind at ease when away from home. You can arm, disarm or simply check on your house from anywhere using the Blink app or via the Alexa Blink smart home skill on any Echo device. Now at an all-time low price on Amazon.

One of Blink's cheapest deals is this Video Doorbell System, which includes a Sync Module Core for secure footage storage. Blink's doorbell has a two-year battery life, meaning you won't have to worry about hardwiring if you're renting. It also has a 150° head-to-toe view, can automatically send you parcel and person alerts, and helps keep your worries at bay with continuous live view.

Now 66% off, Blink has combined its Outdoor 2k+ and Mini 2k+ into an affordable home security package. You'll score two of each camera for the ultimate protection when you're away from home, and you'll get the Blink Sync Module 2, which allows you to store your footage locally.

Better yet, you'll be able to check in on your home and view footage in 2K clear resolution, even at night and zoom in on all the nooks and crannies around your home. What a win.

If you’re keen to fit out your house with the whole kit and caboodle, Blink has discounted the lot and bundled them up for easy purchasing. With a Mini 2, Blink Doorbell and Sync Module Core, it’s an extensive and inexpensive way to cover the entire home. And to top it off, you'll also receive a 30-day free trial of Blink's subscription plan to try it out. What a win.

Nab a new Wi-Fi router with this limited-time eero 7 deal. With 15% off, this two-pack of Wi-Fi 7 modems can support NBN plans with up to 2.5Gbps speeds and over 120 devices with minimal to no interruptions.

The Echo Dot offers impressive audio quality for a smart speaker. While it's not the cheapest we have seen, this smart speaker comes with voice control via Alexa too, so you can stream your favourite apps, listen to music or the news and schedule reminders.

The latest Echo home display devices have gotten a much-needed glow-up in the Echo Show 8 and the Echo Show 11. Aside from the updated in-cell touch and negative liquid crystal screens, both devices include new front-facing stereo speakers and a custom woofer for room-filling spatial audio. The key difference between the two? The Echo Show 8 has a smaller 8.7-inch display.

With all the same great features as the Echo Show 8 above, if you're after a larger home display screen to connect to your Ring devices, check recipes while cooking or control your smart devices using Alexa, then the 11-inch Echo Show could be the move for you.

The Echo Dot Max features almost 3x the bass of the Echo Dot (5th gen), and its sound can automatically adapt to your space, making it the perfect addition to any smart home or party setup. We gave it a nice 4 stars in our review, namely for its great smart home capabilities and stellar sound.

If you're looking to amplify your home streaming set-up, this Fire TV Cube offers lightning-fast app loading thanks to its octa-core processor — which is 2x more powerful than the Fire TV Stick 4K Max. You can stream more than 350k movies and TV shows with access to all of your favourite streamers and free-to-air channels. While it has been cheaper before, the TV Cube is rarely discounted, so this is still a solid deal.

Elevate your home entertainment experience with the Fire TV Stick 4K Plus. This nifty gadget plugs into any TV's HDMI port and allows you to stream Netflix, Binge, Prime Video and more, all from an Alexa-enabled remote. Note that the Fire TV Stick 4K Plus is a new name for the Fire TV Stick 4K, but they are otherwise identical.

Looking to beef up home security but worried about the cost? The Ring Indoor Camera 2 is now massively discounted. Simply plug it into the nearest wall socket, link it up with the Ring app and you'll have access to sharp 1080p video footage within your home. It even comes with a 30-day free trial of Ring Protect, which allows you to keep old footage on file — though you will have to pay a subscription fee after the trial is up if you want to keep said videos. And this is the second-lowest price it's been on Amazon so far.

Knock a nice 30% off this Pan-Tilt camera, designed specifically for pet owners. With a 169° tilt and 360° pan angles, you can monitor every nook and cranny of your home when you're away, and make sure Fido and Tiger don't get up to mischief. Available in both black and white colourways at this all-time low price.

Give your home a doorbell and gain some peace of mind with the newest Ring Video Doorbell (Battery). As the name suggests, it has a built-in rechargeable battery, so you don't need an electrician to install it. That said, you do have the option of wiring it into your home's electrical system if you'd prefer. Provides 24/7 video capture in crystal-clear Retinal 2K and offers 6x zoom. Do note that this discount is exclusive to the Speckled Grey colourway.

Apartment dwellers, rejoice! If you live in a building with an eligible system, Ring's Intercom device can answer the door for packages or people when you're not home, taking the stress off any missed deliveries. Better yet, this deal comes with an Indoor Camera so you can monitor anyone inside (or outside) your home.

Looking for a camera-focused phone without paying Apple or Samsung prices? Xiaomi's 17T 5G offers just that. Its Leica-powered 5x telephoto camera helps you capture sharp shots from near or far, while the huge 6,500mAh battery and 67W fast charging keep you going throughout the day with less time plugged in. Add in a smooth 120Hz display and generous 512GB of storage, and this deal delivers plenty of premium specs for less.

The Pixel 10 Pro may not be Google's latest flagship, but it's still a fantastic buy for anyone after a reliable Android phone at a great price. Expect the clean Pixel software experience, excellent camera performance and powerful AI features that Google's phones are known for. Just know that while this is an international model that's sold by a third party, it still comes with 2 years warranty.

With a 20,000mAh capacity and 20W power delivery, this option from Vrurc is ideal for those who need to extend their phone's battery life well beyond what it's typically capable of, and who don't want to lug around a bulky bank.

This power bank can charge at up to 145W, and has dual USB-C ports, plus a USB-A. You can charge multiple devices at once, including your laptop and phone at the same time.

If you're an Apple user and you want to keep tabs on your luggage, your pet, your house keys or anything else, AirTags are your best bet. These are the original ones, with the 4-pack now down to an all-time low price, just AU$2 off the lowest AU$129 we saw in October.

While we've not reviewed this 75% mechanical gaming keyboard ourselves, reviews from other reputable sources across the web are largely glowing, praising its construction quality, performance and low price. It's even available with two switch styles and a range of six colours.

Want to free up some space on your desk? 65% keyboards are super popular right now, and Asus takes it a step further with low-profile optical switches. A hit with gamers, the discounted Asus ROG Falchion RX features pre-lubed red linear switches and vibrant RGB lighting for an extra touch of flair.

Logitech's Pebble 2 mouse and keyboard combo is a great option for Mac users, offering a blend of style and practicality at an affordable price. These devices connect via a Bluetooth dongle and feature a sleek, ultra-slim design, perfect for portability.

Take your Switch 2 on the go with this portable charging case from Belkin. With enough juice for 1.5 recharges, you can easily extend your playtime no matter where you are.

While this mini home projector has been discounted to this price before on Amazon, it's still a great deal. With 2.5 hours of playtime, up to 120-inch display and 200 ANSI Lumens of brightness, this projector will enhance home movie nights. Our friends at TechRadar gave its predecessor 4.5 stars in their review, so we're confident the next-gen is just as super.

If you're in the market for a Kindle but don't know where to start, this 2024 model is the perfect first e-reader. Designed as the lightest and most compact Kindle, it has a 300ppi high-res display screen, measuring 6 inches. It also has 16GB of storage space for housing thousands of your favourite e-books.

The Kindle Paperwhite standard model is a gorgeous upgrade to your ageing e-reader. With a glare-free display, seven weeks of battery, adjustable light and a waterproof rating, this Kindle can come with you anywhere.

Using a 7-inch E Ink display with support for over 4,000 colours, 16GB storage and up to eight weeks' battery life on a single charge, the Kindle Colorsoft is hard to pass up, especially if you mostly read comics, manga or graphic novels. Now at an all-time low for Black Friday, this is a popular e-reader and one of the best colour models we've seen to date.

With 32GB storage, an auto-adjusting front light and a vibrant colour display, the Kindle Colorsoft Signature improves on the standard edition by adding wireless charging to the mix.

Score a tidy AU$1,000 off this iPad Pro and Apple Pencil Pro this Black Friday. With 2TB of storage space, Wi-Fi and Cellular capability, a nice 11-inch glass display and the superpower processor of the M5 chip, this tablet and pen duo will make a great laptop replacement and then some.

With top-notch audio performance and sound quality that rivals the best wireless earbuds, plus balanced tuning, effective ANC, and impressive battery life, these Sennheiser buds are sure to delight any audiophile.

While slightly more expensive than last Prime Day, these wired earbuds are at a great price. The cable provides a more reliable and stable connection to source devices, though a 3.5mm-to-USB or Lightning adapter will likely be required for phone compatibility. Once connected, they deliver exceptional high-fidelity sound. As expected from Sennheiser, they feature outstanding build quality and offer exceptional comfort for extended listening sessions.

Hey runners, if you're serious about your sport, you may want to consider the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2. These open-ear headphones are built for performance, delivering better bass and a super secure, comfy fit for those long runs. Plus, you can take calls clearly, and the open-ear design means you'll always be aware of what's happening around you.

If swimming is more your thing, the Shokz OpenSwim Pro 2 are excellent for listening to tunes while doing laps. Apart from being IP68 water resistant, they offer 9 hours of listening time and 32GB of storage for MP3s. And thanks to Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity, they're just as good for running.

Available in a fair few colourways at this fantastic discount, the JBL Charge 5 can bring the party, and quite loudly, I might add. I use this Bluetooth speaker at home myself and love it, with up to 20 hours of playback. It's also dust and waterproof (IP67 rating), so you can take it anywhere, plus it will double as a phone charger in a pinch if you need some extra juice on your handset.

The QuietComfort SC headphones offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) performance and sound quality, though they process audio differently and lack the Immersive Audio mode of the premium QuietComfort Ultra. These foldable headphones also come with a soft case. While the SC model is frequently discounted and this offer isn't the lowest price we've seen in July (AU$239.99), it's still a solid deal.

The Bose Ultra Open Earbuds deliver the power and quality you’d expect from Bose, with the added perks of an open-ear design. The immersive sound is top-notch, offering up to seven hours of playtime and as much as 48 hours on standby. They’re reliable, effortless, and perform beautifully. This discount is available in a few colours under the same listing.

Okay, so it's not the most mind-blowing deal we've ever seen, but even a 21% discount on Apple's awesome AirPods Max 2 is definitely worth a look. Now down by AU$211.

Amazon's offering the biggest discount on Apple's third-gen AirPods Pro earphones we've seen to date. Though some of the improvements over their forebears are small, these are still indisputably the best in-ear AirPods ever, with better noise cancellation, fuller bass and crisper treble, plus smart features like live language translation and heart rate monitoring.

The Sennheiser Accentum Wireless cans offer clean sound, even if they aren't as dynamic-sounding as Sennheiser's Momentum headphones, but they do offer impressive ANC and a long 50-hour battery life. Now 51% off, this is the second-lowest price we've seen on these great over-ear cans.

It may not be the biggest discount, but it’s worth a look for its spatial audio, rich soundstage, and dynamic head tracking. Plus, with up to five hours of battery life on a single charge and 30 hours with the included carry case, you can enjoy your music for longer.

Love the thrill of a blind box keyring? The Kodak Charmera is worth getting your hands on. We gave it 4 stars in our review, as it is, simply put, "cute, cheap and lo-fi". You're not going to get high-definition quality out of it, but you'll get a cute keyring camera with vintage aesthetic photos and videos. The Charmera has 11 different filters and frames to choose from, and comes with a USB-C cord for easy charging. You'll only need to add a microSD card with a GB capacity of your choice to transfer your pics. Oh, and your selected colourway? That's anyone's guess, as the Charmera comes in seven mystery colours, including a "secret" rare option.

Capturing 4K content just got cuter with this tiny Insta360 Go 3S camera. It's totally magnetic, so you can stick it to most surfaces and capture 360-degree POVs. With 25% off on Amazon, this bundle is great for budding content creators, adventurers, and risk-takers on the go.

We gave this fully automatic machine a 3-star rating, as we found it was rather ambitious and some of its results were mediocre, but our reviewer said it was relatively easy to use. It might not be for the fanciest of coffee connoisseurs, but if you want the convenience of an automatic espresso machine, this Ninja is a good contender.

Take a nice 38% off one of our top-rated espresso makers. The Breville Bambino Plus is an easy-to-use, compact machine that takes the guesswork out of the perfect espresso shot and steamed milk. Do note, you'll need a grinder to complete your coffee routine.

With a nice saving, it's hard to dismiss this Breville coffee machine deal. The Barista Express has a built-in grinder, tamper, and bean hopper, so there's no need to buy a separate grinder or hand tamp. Available in a few colourways under the same listing.

Equipped with a steam wand, controlled dosage and grind settings and active temperature control, the De'Longhi La Specialista Arte is the perfect beginner-friendly manual machine. It's also compact, meaning it won't take up much bench space, and comes with everything you need to make your perfect brew on the first go. Now discounted by 23%, this is the perfect Black Friday purchase if you're a lover of all things caffeine.

Just AU$1 more than its lowest price ever of AU$87, this Nespresso Vertuo Pop machine is hard to pass up at a massive 62% off in the Solo White colourway. With one-touch convenience, you can brew up to four different cup sizes from a range of great Nespresso coffee pods. You'll also receive a 12-pack of coffee capsule samples to try.

Now at its lowest price in the last month, you can't surpass the one-touch convenience of a Nespresso Vertuo Pop. Now available in this Coconut White colourway on Amazon, with a complimentary coffee pod sample kit and milk frother.

If you want the latest Nespresso model, let me introduce you to the Vertuo Up. With the same great features as the Vertuo Pop range, the Up has a sleek new design, can connect to the accompanying Nespresso Smart App and has a specialised Coffee Creations mode for a more concentrated brews.

While our Nespresso Vertuo Creatista review noted that its price was a concern, this discount significantly lessens that issue. We praised the machine's integrated milk frother and its use of Vertuo pods, which offer various cup and mug sizes. The Creatista is also an excellent performer, capable of brewing your morning coffee exceptionally fast. Do note, this price was AU$100 cheaper yesterday, so it might fluctuate throughout today.

Not the lowest price we've seen, but this 3-in-1 Ninja coffee machine brews quality espresso, drip coffee and even fast cold brew using its Barista Assist technology, an integrated grinder and weight-based dosing. As an iced coffee all-year-round enjoyer, the Ninja Luxe Cafe has changed my life, thanks to its cold-pressed espresso presets and its specialty Dual Froth system with a cold-foam setting.

Using built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth compatibility, you can easily monitor your cooking progress and temperature using Inkbird's BBQ thermometer. The kit comes with two detachable probes, an LCD screen displaying temperature and a charging cord. Made out of food-grade stainless steel, the probes are waterproof, heat-resistant and wear-resistant, meaning they can be popped into the dishwasher after use for easy cleaning.

The Ninja BlendBoss is a sleek, smart, and powerful appliance for enjoying blended drinks on the go. Simply pop in your ingredients to blend, then detach the tumbler from its base to carry it around. With a 1,100W motor, it's more than capable of crushing your favourite smoothie mix, including ice.

We're big fans of the Ninja Slushi on Tom's Guide — it's awesome for everything from frappes to smoothies, and even a boozy slushie if that's your vibe, thanks to its super handy drink modes. Now discounted by 67% — a record Amazon low, beating the previous one of AU$236.55.

If you're keen to get outside and cook this summer, chances are that this deal is for you. This Ninja outdoor pizza oven offers 8 functions, including pizza, max roast, specialty roast and smoker, amongst others, so it’s by no means limited to just pizza.

Roast, bake, or crisp twice as many dishes with Ninja's DoubleStack air fryer tower, now near its all-time low on Amazon. This model houses two independently controlled drawers that can cook up to four different foods at once, all while taking up less counter space than a typical extra-large air fryer. With a massive 9.5L capacity, you can even control the timings so that your meal is done at the exact same time.

Ninja's original glass air fryer packs 1700W of power into a portable design, with two borosilicate glass containers that serve as both frying baskets and serving dishes. The borosilicate means they can also withstand extreme temperatures, making it easy to take your favourite foods from frozen to crispy. The Crispi also comes with two removable crisping grates and two snap-on container lids for easy food storage post-feast.

Want an air fryer and induction cooker all-in-one? Meet Tefal's YumMeal. You can prep, cook, eat and clean in the same bowl, making it perfect for smaller households with minimal storage space.

Tefal's SuperGrill is the answer to all your cooking and grilling needs at home. It can act like an indoor barbecue, grilling your favourite proteins, and it can toast, broil and melt. Now discounted by 50%, if you're looking for a 3-in-1 grill plate, Tefal's SuperGrill is one to consider.

Designed to spot messes the naked eye can miss, the Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal uses light to detect hidden stains and spills on your hard floors. Better yet, it also features a heated mop that can scrub the toughest stains. It's also equipped with LiDAR navigation, an anti-tangle roller brush, eight PowerDetect modes that adapt to your flooring and a NeverTouch Pro Base that handles the debris and self-cleaning for you.

Also available in Eclipse Navy for AU$1,049 or Café Noir Mocha for an extra AU$21.

This Dreame vacuum is a certified steal. With a powerful and long-lasting runtime, its lightweight and compact attachments, and its sleek design, there's a lot to like about this budget stick vac.

If you're looking to save some extra pennies on a stick vac purchase, this deal is for you. The Shark IZ102 cordless vac offers powerful suction and a self-cleaning brush roll. Plus, the nozzle has LED lights that'll reveal any hidden dust and debris as you vacuum.

I've been reviewing this Roborock for the last few weeks and I have never been more obsessed with a robot vacuum — and that's saying something. With impressive 36,000Pa suction, a roller mop, great obstacle avoidance and an anti-tangle brush, this Roborock Saros 20 is one to consider at 33% off.

This Ecovacs Deebot T30s Pro deal shouldn't be swept away. With powerful suction, smart mopping features, anti-tangle technology, and a self-cleaning auto-empty station, the T30s Pro can handle messes on both carpets and hard floors, making it an ideal spring cleaning companion.

If you're after something a little more automated to help you maintain a dust-free living space every day, this Ecovacs could be a top contender. The Ecovacs Deebot N20, this robot comes with 8,000Pa suction power, a tangle-free brush and up to 300 minutes of runtime. It also has the great floor-mapping features Ecovacs is known for, which is a marvellous inclusion at this low price.

Need a totally hands-free vacuum that gets the job done? Meet the Ecovacs X8 Max Pro Omni, which has great suction power, a self-cleaning mop roller and a detangling brush roller.

Talk about a cool deal! Shark's portable tabletop misting fan, the HydroGo, is now discounted. While the Lilac colourway has the biggest discount, it also comes in numerous other super cute pastel colourways (my favourite is Honey Dew) and it weighs less than 2kg for easy transporting. Whether you're headed to the beach, camping or even a picnic, the HydroGo will be your new favourite travelling companion.

The Dreame H15 Pro Heat is a sleek, competent wet/dry vacuum excelling on hard floors. The heated wash mode offers effective cleaning and shiny floors. There's also decent dry cleaning on hard floors.

You'll never have to worry about any wet (or pet) messes at home ever again with the Shark StainStriker. This powerful spot cleaner gets rid of tough stains and spots in a breeze, so much so that you might not even realise there was a mess in the first place.

While we haven't reviewed this particular model, we gave its predecessor, the Shark HydroVac, a massive 4.5 stars in our review, as it proved to be a powerful tool for grime and dirt on both hard and carpeted floors. This model, the XL, is slightly larger, with a bigger capacity for the dirty water tank.

In the market for a wet-dry vac? This Roborock is one to consider. With a blue light to help find hidden debris, 22,000Pa suction power and steam functionality, this Roborock is perfect for every kind of wet (or dry) messes.

One of the latest Tineco flagships, the S7 Artist, is also discounted on Amazon. The newer model has undergone a total redesign, with the clean water tank sitting at the base of the floor washer. Personally, I quite like the colourful LED lights that illuminate the different modes of the machine, which include Auto, Max and Suction, all of which are perfect for tidying wet (or dry) messes.

The Shark NeverChange purifier with a HEPA-certified filter that traps airborne allergens and pollutants; this purifier will ensure you breathe easily and clean deeply, no matter what floats through your home.

Calling all pet owners, parents, and messy eaters, this little machine is for you. Using warm water and stain formula, this carpet washer quickly removes spots and stains from carpets, furniture, rugs and more, with ease. Saving you time and money, this machine is worth every penny.

While the Saucony Triumph 23 is not the most exciting running shoe, it has a couple of key features to recommend it. One is that it's very comfortable and protective, and the other is its durability. That said, it's now discounted by up to 44% in both men's and women's sizes, which is one of the deepest discounts we've seen, so it could be worth nabbing ASAP.

Knocking up to 50% off, these Crocs Classic clogs are extremely versatile, breathable and dry fast when wet, making them perfect for almost every activity. Available in a range of colours under the same listing — and note that some colourways are a little pricier than others.

These Crocs Toe Loop sandals are ideal for summer, providing both style and comfort. Available in a range of sizes and colours under the same listing.

Never heard of Heydude shoes? Well, let me introduce them to you. This Wally style comes with great (and comfy) features, including a flexible outsole, removable insole and stretchy canvas upper.

These Heydude comfy stretch canvas boat-style shoes are totally hands-free, so you can slide them on while you're halfway out the door. They're flexible, lightweight and have a removable insole.

Can't sleep without the dull sound of white noise in the background? You're not alone. If you can't afford a Hatch alarm clock, then this Glocusent is one to consider. It does all the same things — plays white noise, has a dimmable light and smart display — but comes at a fraction of the price. Now discounted to AU$62.99 for Black Friday.

Hitting fitness goals can be tricky, and it always helps to have the right tools in your arsenal to get you there faster. The Homebuds Digital Scales provide accurate results every time, thanks to the in-built auto calibration and weight sensors. The scales come with batteries included and a bright LED screen for displaying results.

Need a new emotional support water bottle? Try this Owala. With insulated stainless steel, it'll keep any of your favourite cold beverages cool for hours at a time, and you can customise your colourway from the various vivid options under the same listing.

Is a tumbler more your speed? Then perhaps you could be persuaded by this style from Owala as well. Complete with an easy-to-carry side handle and spout/straw lid, this tumbler can go everywhere with you.

As a cat mum, I've been using a PetSafe ScoopFree litter box for a few years now, and it's changed my life. I've been watching this SmartSpin version in hopes the AU$599 price would drop, and finally it has. This self-cleaning, spinning litter box sifts away clumps and sends smart alerts when the waste box needs emptying. It even comes with an essential oil spray nozzle, so your home will always stay fresh, regardless of which room the litter box is in.

If you've been worried about your indoor plants dying or your home being too humid, this gadget might help. This Hygrometer will track your home and yard's temperature, humidity, and comfort levels. It'll alert you to any trends or changes, so you can optimise plant growth or air quality in your home.

Say goodbye to expensive laser hair removal clinics, and hello to Braun's IPL machine. This handheld device uses broad-spectrum pulses of light to target hair follicles beneath the skin without breaking the surface. I've been using it for a few weeks now, and while my results are minimal, it's already saved me a few trips to the clinic. I'll report back with my findings soon, but if you've wanted to try an IPL machine at home, don't just take my word for it — Braun's option has gotten several 4-star ratings under this listing.

Never did I ever think I'd enjoy sucking "gunk" out of my face on a Friday evening, but now it's become a crucial part of my weekly routine. This DIY facial machine scored 4 stars in our review: skin is noticeably more radiant after the first use, the DePuffi tool works wonders on tired eyes, and it's quite satisfying to use once you get the hang of it. Now discounted by 25% on Amazon.

If you're invested in your skincare routine, it may be time to spoil yourself with a new addition in the Shark CryoGlow. Using a range of colours to treat different skin concerns, Shark's CryoGlow emits specific wavelengths of light that penetrate the skin at various depths and trigger biological reactions. These light settings are known as four different "treatments", which emit select LED colours to target different skin concerns. Now discounted by 29% on Amazon.

An even cheaper alternative in the hairdryer space is the Dreame Gleam. It has a speedy 110,000 RPM motor, customisable settings and built-in ion technology for a frizz-free finish every time.

I've been using this hair styler from Mova for the past two months now, and it's taken over the top spot that once belonged to my Shark FlexStyle. It features nine great attachments, including Coanda curling wands and a hair essence drying attachment. Now for AU$282, this Mova multi-styler is hard to pass up.

Dreame's Aero Straight Pro slashes hair drying and styling time by combining a dryer and straightener into one airflow-powered tool. With precise, angled airflow and heat settings, it takes wet hair and dries it to a smooth, naturally straight finish, so you don't need multiple tools to complete your routine. Intelligent sensors also help minimise heat damage. Now 50% off, this powerful styler is well worth snapping up at its discounted price.

With up to 64% off, this Oral-B toothbrush will keep your pearly whites clean, removing up to 100% more plaque than a regular toothbrush. It has three gentle brushing modes and has a long-lasting battery.

Shark's latest airstyler, the Glam, is a notable improvement on the Flexstyle, incorporating new styling attachments to make it a 4-in-1 styler. You'll need to act fast to grab this 5-star rated styler, as it's sure to sell out at this discounted rate!

If you need a new hairdryer, but don't require all the bells and whistles of a Dyson Supersonic or Shark Speedstyle, then this Remington Aero 2000 is a great option. The Remington dryer packs a 2000W motor that's ideal for fast drying and styling if you're in a hurry. It comes with two styling attachments and has 3 different heat settings, including a cool shot for setting your blowout.

Save on Shark's latest hair tool, the Glossi. Using airflow, heat and ceramic, the Glossi promises to deliver frizz-free shine and volume to any hairstyle, without major heat damage. What a win.

This stunning 6,020-piece Lego Harry Potter Hogwarts Castle set, including 4 minifigures, gives fans a glimpse into the microscale world of Harry Potter — but beware of the Basilisk! With hours of interactive play, muggles will be spellbound with this enchanting set.

Lego's Super Mario The Mighty Bowser is a 2807-piece build with a button-activated head, neck movement and a fireball shooter. Standing over 32cm tall, the buildable character model and battle platform is a must-have for any Super Mario fan.

Cat lovers, rejoice! Finally, a Lego set that represents the feline friend in all of us, this adorable creature is the purrfect companion to any home decor. Available with yellow and blue eyes in the box, this Lego cat is designed with a posable head, tail and paws.

#3141. Google Play will show some app developers’ home addresses to the world

The EU only requires the details for European buyers, but Google plans to display them everywhere.

Google Play will show traders’ contact details worldwide from March 2027.

Play Store developers must tell Google by February 1, 2027, whether they are traders under the EU’s Digital Services Act. From March 1, Google will show traders’ contact details worldwide, which for personal accounts means a physical address and phone number. Apple shows them only in the EU.

Google will start showing the contact details of many Play Store developers to users worldwide next year, Digital Trends reported. For some who publish apps as individuals, that means their home address.

Developers must tell Google by February 1, 2027, whether they count as “traders” under the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA). Google treats developers who make money from apps as traders, for example through paid downloads, in-app purchases or regular ad revenue. Those who don’t declare a status risk having updates blocked or apps removed.

From March 1, Google will show traders’ contact details on the Play Store. For developers with a personal account, that means a physical address and a phone number. Google won’t accept P.O. boxes, and the address comes from the developer’s payments profile.

The DSA only requires these details to be shown to buyers in the EU. Google plans to show them to everyone.

Apple, which must follow the same EU rules, takes a narrower approach. It shows trader details only in the EU and lets developers list a P.O. box if they can document it.

Developers who don’t distribute apps in the European Economic Area or the UK can declare themselves non-traders. That leaves little room for solo developers who earn money in Europe to keep their home address private.

The change comes as Google opens Play to more first-time developers. Last month, it said anyone could publish apps for free using its AI Studio. In August, a US judge also told Google to stop making rival app stores hard to install.

#3138. WhatsApp launches highly requested new feature for sending messages later

WhatsApp just announced that it is rolling out scheduled messages, which it says is one of users’ most requested features. Here are the details.

From WhatsApp’s blog post announcing support for scheduled messages:

You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats.

To schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. It will look like any other message to the person receiving it. You can see all future messages you have lined up, and delete them beforehand if you change your mind.

Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us.

WhatsApp says this feature is “rolling out globally over the coming weeks.” So you might not see it right away, but even if you don’t, it should show up on your account soon.

Scheduled messages work not only for text, but also when sending media like photos and videos.

Shifting spend from traffic subsidies into rural delivery networks is a bet on reach, not just cheaper prices.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:01PM EST

10 stocks we like better than PDD Holdings ›

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 19, 2026, PDD (PDD +0.23%) announced that it is expanding support for merchants beyond platform operations directly into manufacturing and supply chain infrastructure. For long-term investors, this strategic pivot from short-term marketing spend to deep infrastructure upgrades shows management's focus on building durable operational moats. Strengthening supply chain capabilities directly protects merchant retention and customer loyalty against lower-cost rivals. Three takeaways from management's call stand out.

PDD is shifting resources away from basic traffic subsidies to fund research and development (R&D), manufacturing, and fulfillment capabilities across industrial clusters. Partnering directly with factories allows merchants to establish proprietary brands and improve operational efficiency.

PDD is expanding its free-shipping-to-villages initiative to address last-mile delivery bottlenecks in remote agricultural regions. Covering transport costs from county transit hubs to rural pickup points opens untapped consumer demand and drives merchant order volume.

Management remains focused on strategic investments under its 100 Billion Support Program rather than quarterly expense ratios. PDD prioritizes long-term supply chain resilience over short-term marketing campaigns to maintain consumer trust and platform competitiveness.

Domestic e-commerce competition remains fierce as buyers evaluate prices across platforms. PDD is strengthening supply chain infrastructure, rural fulfillment, and merchant governance to protect market share.

Evolving overseas trade policies create friction for cross-border sellers. Management is expanding warehouse partnerships and local fulfillment infrastructure to build supply chain resilience.

#3136. iOS 27.3 release date: Here’s when new iPhone features are coming

iOS 27.3 is coming soon, packed with new features for iPhone users. Here’s when to expect the next big iPhone software update.

If you follow Apple closely, the company’s software release patterns quickly become clear.

For example, iOS 27.2 launched late last month around the same time as releases in years past. The only difference is that normally iOS 27.1 would launch in late October rather than 27.2. But since Apple made iOS 27.1 exclusive to iPhone Duo, all software releases for the iOS 27 cycle will be off by one number—despite following the same timing as ever.

That means iOS 27.3 is up next, and its release should align with historic patterns for x.2 updates.

Apple has confirmed that iOS 27.3 will launch to all users in December once beta testing concludes.

To get more precise though, here’s a sampling of release patterns for comparable x.2 updates the last few years:

Based on this pattern, iOS 27.3 is expected to release by mid-December.

Apple always tries to ship its last software update of the year with a little buffer before taking a holiday break. That way if any major issues arise, the company can develop a quick fix and push it out before much of the company takes time off.

Expect to see iOS 27.3 launch as early as the week of December 7, or on Monday, December 14 at the latest.

iOS 27.3 is packed with lots of new features for iPhone users spanning various popular apps.

iPhone Duo also benefits from three exciting new features, including face unlock, Reachability, and a new setting to automatically lock the device when closed.

Finally, iOS 27.3 brings the first Apple Intelligence features to China—though Siri AI is still missing.

But this year, I've also rigorously tested two other impressive all-foam: the SweetNight CoolNest and the CopperFlex Essential.

Like many of the beds found in this year's best mattress guide, a memory foam mattress should feature foam layers that delivers body-cradling comfort — and these three affordable options offered me just that during testing. However, while the mattresses are all ideal for side sleeping, there are key differences between them.

In this Sweetnight CoolNest vs EGOHOME Black vs CopperFlex Essential comparison guide, I'll draw on my own experience of lab testing and sleeping on each mattress to explore the differences in price, designs, and comfort. That way, you can make an informed decision when you're looking for a mattress under $500 for a queen in this month's Black Friday mattress sales.

All three of these mattresses are under $500 in a queen this Black Friday, with the EGOHOME and SweetNight always coming in at less than $400 in a queen (which puts them in the budget price tier). Meanwhile, the price of a queen CopperFlex Essential is between $400 and $600, depending on what sale is on. Either way, the CopperFlex is a mid-range bed.

You don't need to be super strategic about when you buy yourself a SweetNight CoolNest, as a queen is pretty much always $399.99 (I've yet to see it on sale for a different price). However, if you time your purchase right, you can often snag two free pillows (worth $100) with your CoolNest bed. We saw this deal during the Labor Day mattress sales, and I'm hoping it may return as Black Friday draws closer.

The EGOHOME is the cheapest of the bunch, and is now $379 for a queen (MSRP is $559, but it's always on sale). However, during holiday sales, you can generally enter a promo code at checkout to knock an extra 10% off the sale price. Basically, if you see 30% off at Brooklyn Bedding, you know you're getting the top deal. With the current 30% discount, a queen CopperFlex Essential is now $489.30 (it's over $500 during the 25% off sales).

As for extras, the CopperFlex Essential boasts the most generous benefits: a year-long sleep trial, a lifetime warranty, and free shipping. EGOHOME and SweetNight also provide free shipping, but their trials and warranties are slightly shorter. However, that's not a complaint — a 10-year warranty and a 100-night sleep trial are perfectly sufficient.

The 12" CoolNest Memory Foam Mattress is $399.99 in a queen right now, which isn't anything new. However, there is a chance that you may snag some freebies as we get closer to Black Friday, as we saw free pillows during Labor Day. Whenever you buy, though, expect a 10-year warranty and 100-night sleep trial.

With the EGOHOME code PREVIEW 10, you can take a queen size EGOHOME Black 12" Foam mattress from $379 (MSRP:$559) down to $341.10. This is excellent value for money, and you can also receive a 10-year warranty and a 100-night sleep trial.

Brooklyn Bedding has ditched its standard 25% discount for Black Friday and rolled out its big 30% off sale. This dunks a queen size CopperFlex Essential under $500, with a queen now $489.30. Thanks to a huge shakeup to 3Z brand's mattress extras, the CopperFlex now comes with a lifetime warranty and one-year trial.

Like the best memory foam mattresses on the market, all three beds are made entirely of foam (not a spring nor coil in sight) and are fiberglass-free.

The 12" SweetNight's design is focused on cooling, with an airflow-enhancing '3D' cover that my fellow testers and I found to be extremely cool-to-the-touch (but more on that later). Its foam is also infused with Phase Change Material (PCM), a specialist cooling fabric found in some of the best cooling mattresses. PCM has been proven to improve human heat dissipation up to 25.6% compared to conventional mattresses

The 12" EGOHOME does have a graphene-infused cover that the brand calls "cooling", but this is very basic. That said, the EGOHOME has an excellent quality build, packed with dense layers of foam (including a EGOHOME's trademarked BraceSleeper Support Foam, which is high-density for extra durability).

Despite being mid-range rather than budget, the CopperFlex has the least sophisticated design out of the three mattresses, with just a copper-infused foam for temperature control. However, its cover does boast a "Nano Stain Terminator Protector" cover to safeguards against stains and spills, plus it comes in a wide range of sizes (including an Olympic queen and RV sizes).

I found all three beds to be good choices for anyone seeking the best mattress for side sleepers (and I say that as a primary side sleeper), but each did boast different levels of pressure relief.

In my SweetNight CoolNest mattress review, I found that the CoolNest provided excellent pressure relief for side and back sleeping (both in objective and subjective tests). It has enough give in the shoulder and hip region to relieve the side-sleeper pressure points, but its ultra-quick response time means it's easy to move around on and avoids that "quicksand" feel that some memory foam mattresses have.

I conducted the EGOHOME Black 12" Foam mattress review for seven months (the longest I've tested a mattress at home) and found it delivered excellent medium-firm support for all sleep positions. However, another tester (a stomach sleeper) considered it a little too soft for front sleeping, proving that mattress firmness is subjective. That said, back and side sleepers should feel both comfortable and supported.

As for the CopperFlex Essential, it's clear from our tests that it's strictly for side sleepers. I found it incredibly cushioning when sleeping on it for my Brooklyn Bedding CopperFlex Essential mattress review, which is surprising as it doesn't have a pillow top. It scored the highest pressure relief score out of the three mattresses, but my fellow testers and I agreed that it's too plush for stomach sleeping.

From the moment I unboxed the SweetNight CoolNest, I found it to be incredibly cool to the touch. I even slept on it through summer heatwaves without AC and it still delivered optimal temperature regulation. My experience was backed up by our thermal imaging camera tests, which found that the SweetNight has a rapid cooling rate of 2.1°F per minute (a cooling rate even quicker than the Bear Elite's 1.82°F per minute).

In contrast, I found that both the CopperFlex Essential and the EGOHOME Black retained heat, especially in the back and shoulder region. Out of the three mattresses, the EGOHOME absorbed the highest amount of heat (15.6°F ), which was definitely noticeable to both me and fellow tester, Ruth Jones. And while the CopperFlex Essential absorbed up to 11.1°F in comparison, its temperature control will pose a problem for hot sleepers.

✅ You want cooler nights: The SweetNight boasts a cool-to-the-touch cover and heat-dissipating PCM which provides a cooler sleep even during hot weather.

✅ You sleep on your side or back: Its medium-firm foam is soft enough to soothe side sleepers but supportive enough for back sleepers. Plus, it's responsive enough for you to change position without feeling 'stuck' in the foam.

✅ You want the best value for money: The EGOHOME Black 12" Foam is the cheapest option, with promo codes adding extra discount to already cheap sale prices.

✅ You're a combination sleeper: I found it to be supportive in all sleep positions, and the medium-firm feel is ideal for side and back sleeping.

✅ You want the most cushioning: Its plush pressure relief is ideal for dedicated side sleepers, even if it's not such a great choice for back and stomach sleepers.

✅ You want generous extras: With a lifetime warranty and a trial that lasts a full year, the CopperFlex boasts the best benefits.

#3134. Report: Apple gains ground as Latin American smartphone shipments plunge 24% in Q3

According to a new Counterpoint Research report, Apple increased its share of Latin America’s smartphone shipments in Q3 2026, recording the smallest decline among the region’s top five brands. Here are the details.

In a report released this week, Counterpoint Research says the ongoing memory crunch led to a 24% year-over-year drop in smartphone shipments during Q3, “the second-lowest quarter since 2015.”

Per the report, Samsung maintained its lead with a 35% shipment share, despite a 15% year-over-year decline in total shipments, well ahead of second-place Motorola, which captured 18% of shipments after a 23% drop. Interestingly, Motorola’s share actually increased one percentage point from a year earlier.

Rounding out the top five were Xiaomi, with a 14% share and a whopping 34% decline, Apple, with a 9% share and a 10% decline, and Honor, with an 8% share and a 27% decline.

Despite the decline in overall shipments, Apple’s shipment share increased by 2 percentage points from 7% a year earlier, moving the company from fifth to fourth place in the region.

Other brands collectively accounted for 16% of shipments, down from 19% a year earlier, with their combined shipments falling 37% year over year.

Here’s Counterpoint on Apple’s performance for Q3 in Latin America:

Apple was the most resilient, with the smallest decline among the top five brands (shipments down 10% YoY), and rose one position to No. 4 in the region. Apple absorbed the impact of price increases better than its rivals, helped by strong product availability. Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro series at the end of the quarter. For the first time, Chile joined Brazil and Mexico in the first launch wave.

As for regional factors that contributed to the decline, Senior Analyst Benjamin Corona noted that Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia faced additional challenges beyond the global memory shortage, ranging from political uncertainty to inflation and tighter household budgets. Smartphone shipments fell 22%, 26%, and 28% in those countries, respectively.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint says it “expects the decline to ease in Q4 2026 as prices stabilize and seasonal demand returns,” adding that “memory-related price pressure should moderate by Q2 2027, but supply constraints will likely continue through the end of 2027.”

Apple TV (now $6.99/month for Black Friday) won big at this year’s Emmy Awards thanks to Widow’s Bay, and this week at the International Emmys, the streamer triumphed again as Carême won the top Drama Series prize.

Apple TV had a record-breaking year at the Emmy Awards this fall, with 29 wins overall—beating HBO as the most-awarded network.

Apple TV’s acclaimed and provocative French hit “Carême” won Drama Series, marking the second time Apple has landed the coveted award following a win in 2024 for “Drops of God.” Recently renewed for a second season and currently filming in Paris, “Carême” stars César Award winner Benjamin Voisin and is directed by Martin Bourboulon.

Carême is based on the book “Carême: The First Celebrity Chef” by Ian Kelly. It premiered on Apple TV last spring and was acclaimed by critics, garnering a 95% Rotten Tomatoes score.

The show follows the story of Antonin Carême, who “rose from humble beginnings in Paris to the height of culinary stardom in Napoleon’s Europe.” Per Apple: “While he dreams only of becoming the most famous chef in the world, his talent and ambitions attract the attention of renowned and powerful politicians who use him as a spy for France.”

Season 2 of Carême was announced earlier this fall, and is expected to premiere in 2027.

I loved Carême’s first season and definitely recommend checking it out if you’re up for a French-language series.

#3131. TDK will spend $635M to double sensor output for robots and AI data centres

The Apple supplier says demand for its magnetic sensors has passed a tipping point.

A TDK factory in Nikaho, Japan. The company plans to double output of its TMR sensors by 2031.

Japan’s TDK plans to invest $635M to double output of its tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) sensors by 2031, Bloomberg reported. The sensors, used in iPhones, are now in demand for cars, humanoid robots and AI data centres, and TDK estimates it makes 80% of the world’s supply.

Japan’s TDK plans to invest $635M to double its output of high-end magnetic sensors by 2031, as demand grows from cars, humanoid robots and AI data centres, Bloomberg reported.

The parts, known as tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) sensors, are precise and use little power. Apple’s iPhones use them for features like camera stabilisation. TDK estimates it makes 80% of the world’s supply.

Takao Tsutsui, who runs TDK’s sensor unit, said demand is already stretching capacity. He added that TDK could invest more if growth speeds up.

“We’ve now passed a tipping point. We now see significant demand ahead,” Tsutsui told Bloomberg.

Each humanoid robot uses dozens of TMR sensors, a TDK spokesperson said. Chinese firms, which build almost every humanoid shipped today, are already retooling phone factories to make more. In data centres, the sensors help adjust power flows as computing loads change and watch over liquid-cooling systems.

TDK, which made its name with cassette tapes, has largely missed out on the AI boom so far. Rivals Murata and Taiyo Yuden have done better, as AI servers soak up so many parts that carmakers face capacitor shortages. TDK’s shares have given up all their gains this year.

The extra output will come from a new plant in Niigata prefecture, which TDK said in June would open in 2029. Customers asked TDK to make sensors outside its existing plant in Nagano, as it is often their only supplier.

“We almost always end up being the sole supplier of TMR sensors,” Tsutsui said.

Others are chasing the same market. Germany’s Infineon is expanding into magnetic sensors, and Bosch is giving its chip and sensor business its own division.

#3130. The Buffett Indicator Is Flashing Red. These 2 Dividend Stocks Could Be Safe Havens.

The Buffett indicator is well above its long-term average, so you may want to consider buying stocks of companies that sell things people don't want to live without.

By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:05PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Johnson & Johnson ›

Johnson & Johnson (JNJ -0.91%) and Procter & Gamble (PG +0.44%) sell products that are bought in both good times and bad. That's notable right now because the so-called Buffett indicator is more than two standard deviations above its historical average, suggesting a high risk of a downturn. If you are a conservative investor, safe-haven stocks in the healthcare and consumer staples sectors should be high on your wish list. Here's why.

Warren Buffett was the former CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.54%)(BRKB +0.37%). His long-term investment approach resulted in the company achieving incredible long-term returns for investors. A key piece of the story was his penchant for waiting to buy until stock prices were attractive. That meant holding off during periods of overvaluation. The tool he used to determine the valuation of the broader market was the total value of the stock market divided by gross domestic product (GDP).

It is a rough gauge, at best. But when the Buffett indicator is at an extreme level, as it is today, it's worth taking a step back. You may want to reevaluate your portfolio, perhaps holding more cash. Or, if you want to remain invested, increasing your exposure to more conservative dividend stocks that have a history of holding up during periods of economic and market weakness. That's exactly what you'll find with J&J and P&G.

One of the big reasons to like J&J right now is that it is a Dividend King, with the longest dividend streak of any healthcare company at 64 years. It has successfully navigated multiple recessions and bear markets over that span. While the company has changed over the years, it currently focuses on the pharmaceutical and medical device segments of the broader healthcare sector.

The big story is that drugs and medical devices usually aren't optional purchases. Consumers are willing to pay for them because they improve their lives and can sometimes mean the difference between life and death. That makes J&J very resilient, a fact bolstered by its diversification across two business lines.

The one problem is valuation. J&J isn't cheap right now, but for conservative investors, it may be worth paying a premium if the lofty level of the Buffett indicator has you worried. That said, the healthcare giant's 1.9% dividend yield is well above the 1% you'd collect from the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.25%) and the healthcare average of roughly 1.3%.

P&G is one of the world's largest consumer staples companies. It has a strong brand portfolio focused on paper products, toiletries, and makeup. Most of its products sit at the high end of their categories, which would seem like a risky place to be during an economic downturn. However, P&G has long focused on innovation, producing products that consumers are willing to pay more for. Notably, despite belt-tightening in many households today, P&G's organic sales grew 4% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

And consumers aren't likely to stop buying their favorite toilet paper and toothpaste even if there is a downturn. At least that's what history has shown, helping P&G to increase its dividend for 70 consecutive years. Like J&J, that's the best streak in its peer group.

P&G isn't exactly cheap, either. However, its price-to-sales and price-to-earnings ratios are roughly in line with their five-year averages. That suggests the stock is fairly valued right now. And the stock's 2.5% yield is above the consumer staples average of 2%, so you are getting a generous yield.

The Buffett indicator is flashing bright red warning signs right now, given its elevated level. If that has you thinking about dialing back on risk, you should consider reliable dividend stocks from defensive sectors like healthcare and consumer staples. The best dividend records in those two sectors belong to Johnson & Johnson and Procter & Gamble. It's probably a good idea to start your search with these two safe-haven stocks.

Whether you’re new to Xbox and want to build out your game library or want to upgrade your console with some new accessories, now is the best time to do so. Here are the best Black Friday Xbox deals worth shopping right now.

The Xbox Series S is limited to 1440p output but still delivers fast loading, ray tracing, and high frame rates. It features a GPU with up to 4 teraflops of output, 10GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. This console has no disc drive; it's designed exclusively for digital games.

The Xbox Series X All-Digital is the same powerful console with two key differences. Firstly, it comes in an attractive Robot White hue, and it also lacks a disc drive, so it is designed solely for digital play. It's the perfect console for Xbox Game Pass players.

If you miss chatting with friends the old fashioned way on Xbox Live, then this keyboard accessory that attaches to your Xbox controller could be the perfect way to relive the glory days. It works with the Xbox Series X/S controllers as well as with older Xbox one S and one Elite controllers. There’s also a 3.5mm audio jack if you want to plug in a wired headset at the bottom too.

While the Xbox Series X25 Limited Edition console is hard to come by and expensive, this deal lets you celebrate Xbox’s big anniversary for less. The GameSir X5 Lite is officially licensed by Xbox and supports phones or even small tablets like the iPad mini. This mobile game controller has Hall Effect sticks and triggers to prevent stick drift and you can swap its face buttons to match your preferred layout.

Versatile, comfortable, and responsive, the Xbox Core Wireless Controller impressed us in our rigorous testing. This isn't just for Xbox — it's compatible with PC, Android, and iOS devices too. With its ergonomic design, textured grips, and a button to share screenshots with friends, it's a go-to for gamers everywhere.

The Arctis Nova 5 is one of the finest gaming headsets, and it's the highest-scoring headset we've reviewed. Compatible with PS5, Nintendo Switch, PC, Android, iOS and Meta Quest, its quick-switch 2.4GHz dongle and Bluetooth 5.3 enable you to effortlessly swap between devices. The sound quality is incredible, and the 360° spatial audio makes your gaming experiences even more immersive.

This modular wired controller lets you swap out its thumbstick modules completely tool free. It also has two remappable buttons around back along with trigger stops. The eSwap Pro has mechanical face buttons too as well as a mechanical D-pad for enhanced precision, comfort and control. You may be tethered to your Xbox, but you’ll have pro-level control in the games you play.

This wireless headset is available in black or white and lets you connect to your Xbox, PC or smartphone using the included 2.4 GHz Hyperspeed Wireless Gen 2 dongle, Bluetooth or over USB-C. The BlackShark V3 also has a detachable Super Wideband mic and delivers excellent virtual surround sound on both Xbox and PC. It's worth noting that the black version is only slightly discounted at $127.

Grand Theft Auto VI + Xbox Wireless Gaming Controller: was $144 now $122 @ Amazon

This bundle gets you a copy of the standard edition of Grand Theft Auto VI alongside an Xbox Wireless Gaming Controller in Carbon Black. Normally, GTA 6 would cost $80 on its own while the controller would cost $65 so you’re actually saving quite a bit with this deal. You also get to play the biggest game of the decade with a brand new controller too.

The Nacon Revolution X Unlimited Controller is a high-end pad designed for the Xbox Series consoles and PC. It packs pro features like hall effect sticks, adjustable triggers, mappable back buttons, a customizable LC screen, and a rechargeable battery. At $199, it's not a cheap investment, but if you take your Xbox gaming seriously, it's a worthwhile upgrade.

The Turtle Beach Stealth 700 Gen 3 may be a tad bulky, but it delivers outstanding sound quality and a reliable microphone, making it a standout gaming headset. This is an ideal headset for multiplatform users thanks to its dual USB transmitters and fantastic onboard options. It’s one of the best Turtle Beach headsets you can buy, and it can be yours for under $200.

Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds is one of the most memorable entries in the Sonic the Hedgehog series. Packed with chaos, fun, and a bit of a learning curve, CrossWorlds shines with smooth drifting and air tricks that deliver significant boosts.

The latest game in the Mafia series takes you back to 1900s Sicily, the birthplace of organized crime. You play Enzo, a fresh recruit in the Torrisi crime family, and must work your way up the ranks to become a "made man." Offering a narrative-driven campaign packed with third-person firefights and high-speed chases (in cars and on horseback), Mafia: The Old Country is a highly engaging action-adventure game.

Assassin’s Creed Shadows delivers on its promise of bringing back classic stealth mechanics while introducing new ones and combining the best of the older and RPG titles. The detailed open world of feudal Japan feels alive, with compelling playable and non-playable characters, and varied fighting tactics enrich the combat. But the game struggles to balance its two playable protagonists, and player choices are still inconsequential.

Resident Evil Requiem combines elements from prior installments to deliver one of the strongest entries yet. Though it doesn’t take risks, its thrilling gameplay and stunning graphics keep you engaged from beginning to end.

Pragmata is a breath of fresh air thanks to its tactical combat, clever puzzles, and earnest sci-fi story. It proves that there's still innovation in the AAA space and is yet another winner from Capcom. This is a game that humans and androids alike can enjoy.

Star Wars Zero Company is a new turn-based tactics game where you recruit and lead a squad of operators and experience an original Star Wars story set during the Clone Wars. Offering strategic combat, cinematic production values, and a focus on player decisions, it's one of the best Star Wars video games in ages and a potential GOTY pick.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight takes everything folks know about Batman from popular culture and filters it through the tried-and-true Lego formula. Whether you're a fan of Batman or Lego games, there's a lot to love in this charming adventure.

Control Resonant surpasses its excellent predecessor with a larger scope, both narratively and in gameplay. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging, while the various skill trees offer deep customization. Aside from some confusing maps, this is an almost perfect action-based title.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a dark, brilliantly written vampire RPG with a superb prologue, a memorable cast, and inventive powers. Repetitive combat, a rough performance, and an insipid lead drag it down at times. A flawed, fascinating debut with cult classic written all over it — one that needs some post-launch patches, but kept us hooked regardless.

Step into the cockpit, take flight, and prepare for battle in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, the latest installment in the popular aerial combat franchise. Boasting a full single-player campaign and the series largest suite of online modes to date, not to mention stunning visuals and sound, it's the complete Ace Combat package.

007 First Light is the finest James Bond video game in nearly 30 years. Its cinematic single-player campaign is remarkable, delivering a gripping, quintessentially Bond story paired with some of the best action-adventure set pieces we’ve ever experienced. Whether you’re a longtime Bond fan or a newcomer, 007 First Light is unmissable.

Crimson Desert is one of the most ambitious single-player open-world games ever. It throws a ton of deep systems at you with almost no hand-holding, but once it clicks, the combat feels fantastic, and exploration feels rewarding. There’s enough content here to keep you busy for months on end. The story is pretty average, and the beginning can be brutal, but if you love big sandbox adventures, this one is worth the ride (and $69).

#3127. Major developers, legal experts, and 32 states back Epic in Apple’s SCOTUS appeal

In a significant development in Apple’s Supreme Court appeal of a civil contempt ruling, Epic Games has received backing from 32 states and the District of Columbia, along with major developers, legal experts, former federal judges, and more. Here are the details.

Apple’s ever-sprawling fight against Epic Games over its App Store policies is currently being fought on two fronts: in the Supreme Court, where Apple is seeking to overturn a civil contempt ruling, and in the district court, where the companies are disputing what commission, if any, Apple can charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

The civil contempt ruling came after Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers found that Apple had violated an earlier injunction issued in its App Store dispute with Epic.

In a nutshell, after she ordered Apple to allow developers to direct users to alternative payment methods outside the App Store, the company responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.

Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn the civil contempt ruling, basically arguing that the original injunction did not explicitly prohibit the commissions and other restrictions it imposed on external purchases.

After the Ninth Circuit upheld the contempt finding and denied its request for rehearing, Apple took the case to the Supreme Court, which agreed to hear its appeal.

Importantly, the Supreme Court will only consider the legal standard used to uphold Apple’s civil contempt ruling, not the separate question of what commission, if any, the company can charge on purchases made through external payment methods.

That will still be determined in the district court, where proceedings have continued despite Apple’s attempts to put them on hold pending the Supreme Court’s decision.

With oral arguments scheduled for January 11, 2027, the case has recently seen a flurry of activity, including Apple’s opening brief in September and Epic’s response earlier this month.

Apple also received support from several organizations in September, including the Washington Legal Foundation, the International Center for Law and Economics, the Computer & Communications Industry Association, and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. The US government also submitted a brief supporting neither party, arguing that the contempt finding was unjustified over Apple’s 27% commission, but warranted over its restrictions on button designs.

Which brings us to the latest developments: a series of amicus briefs filed in support of Epic Games.

Last week, a total of 9 amicus briefs were filed in support of Epic Games, including one led by Utah and joined by 31 other states and the District of Columbia.

This particular brief notes that “the district court correctly held Apple in contempt for continuing to engage in anticompetitive conduct barred by a prior injunction,” adding:

“The court found that Apple engaged in unlawful anti-steering restrictions and required Apple to lift those restrictions. Apple then lifted them in name only, imposed new (and substantially similar) strictures on developers that mirrored the old ones and produced the same result. Worse still, Apple did all this in bad faith: Apple knew its behavior was wrong and actively hid that fact from the court, including by providing false testimony. Under any reasonable reading of the district court’s injunction, Apple’s conduct is worthy of civil contempt.”

The states also argue that “Injunctions in competition cases cannot afford complete relief without addressing the ongoing effects of anticompetitive behavior,” and that “[c]onstruing competition injunctions narrowly defeats their purpose and prevents meaningful redress.”

Similar arguments appear throughout the other briefs, which include submissions from Spotify, Match Group, and Microsoft, as well as nonprofit organizations such as the American Antitrust Institute (AAI), Public Knowledge, and the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF).

In their joint brief, Spotify, Match Group, and Microsoft argue that they “have first-hand experience with the effects of Apple’s conduct and evasion efforts,” adding that “Apple’s new restrictions were no different from the unlawful rules they replaced.”

As for the brief filed by former federal judges, they warned that “[i]n cases like these, where enjoined parties seek to circumvent an injunction through reliance on its literal text, courts must have the power of contempt to deter and remedy evasion. Otherwise, courts would be forced into a game of whack-a-mole, trying to anticipate every possible means of evading an injunction […]”

Arguments by the Little Tech Association, AAI, Public Knowledge, and the EFF all follow a similar line, with some also addressing how Apple’s restrictions on external payment links could affect consumer choice, pricing, and competition.

#3126. I'd Buy Anthropic Stock Early — but Only If I Liked the Answers to These 3 Questions

The AI lab's revenue is soaring, but the outlook for its profitability and valuation will determine whether the stock is worth buying at current prices.

By Manali Pradhan, CFA – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:17PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›

Anthropic (ANT +1.08%), the company behind the Claude AI ecosystem, priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share. However, when trading began on Nov. 19, the stock opened at $111.50, a 34.3% premium to that price. Shares closed at $81.90 on Nov. 24, leaving investors who bought at the opening price with a loss of over 26%.

Still, investor interest in the stock is high. Nearly seven in 10 stock investors surveyed by The Motley Fool said they planned to buy OpenAI, Anthropic, or both at their IPOs.

However, there are three specific questions that investors will want to answer before buying Anthropic stock.

Anthropic's revenue surged more than tenfold from $1.38 billion in the third quarter of 2025 to $16.96 billion in the third quarter of 2026. The number of customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue for Anthropic also increased from more than 950 to over 11,900 in the same time frame. The company had more than 1,900 customers that spent at least $1 million with it on an annualized basis at the end of the third quarter. This indicates that businesses are increasingly spending substantial amounts on the Claude AI ecosystem.

However, Anthropic's revenue depends heavily on customer usage. Consumption-based fees accounted for approximately 79% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026. When businesses expand their use of Claude Code and other applications, they generate more revenue for Anthropic. However, customers could also reduce spending by limiting their token use or by switching to lower-priced AI models or competing services.

Anthropic reported net revenue retention of approximately 900% at the end of September. This highlights the rapid spending growth among the company's existing customers. However, that calculation includes customers who generated as little as $1 in revenue in the prior-year quarter. Hence, the 900% figure may partly reflect rapid expansion from a low starting base rather than a growth rate Anthropic can sustain.

Pricing is another concern. Anthropic disclosed that price reductions and contractual discounts that it introduced in the second and third quarters cut its revenue by approximately $600 million.

With OpenAI's ChatGPT, Alphabet's (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%) Gemini, and other artificial intelligence (AI) competitors competing for enterprise customers, Anthropic will need to maintain strong usage growth without sacrificing too much on pricing.

Anthropic reported an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter, compared with a $974 million profit in the second quarter. However, adjusted operating income increased from $2.24 billion to $2.46 billion. The adjusted figure excludes stock-based compensation and certain other expenses paid in shares rather than cash. Such payments do reduce other shareholders' ownership stakes in the company.

Computing expenses were a major concern. Anthropic's revenue increased sequentially by $5.4 billion in the third quarter, while computing and infrastructure expenses rose by $4.3 billion. Hence, the increase in computing costs was equivalent to nearly 80% of the additional revenue.

Adjusted operating income, however, increased by only $228 million during the same period. Hence, investors need to consider just what fraction of Anthropic's future revenue growth will drop down to the bottom line as profits.

Anthropic's adjusted operating margin declined from 19% in the second quarter to 15% in the third quarter, mainly due to $5 billion in costs associated with leasing computing capacity under expensive short-term deals. The company expects to replace some of that with capacity from cheaper long-term arrangements. However, its continued payments for computing infrastructure could put pressure on cash flow.

Anthropic has firm commitments to spend approximately $900.9 billion on leasing computing and infrastructure, $451.6 billion of which is expected to be spent by the end of 2030. These commitments extend over several years, with some subject to conditions or termination rights.

Anthropic generated $6.57 billion in operating cash flow during the first nine months of 2026. However, it also spent $2.88 billion on equipment purchases and prepayments for leased assets and equipment. Hence, investors should watch whether Anthropic can generate enough cash from operations to fund its growing infrastructure needs.

Anthropic had a market capitalization of approximately $1.1 trillion as of the close of trading on Nov. 24. Hence, the stock was trading at about 31 times its trailing-12-month revenue of $35.28 billion. The valuation multiple drops to around 13.4 times when using Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate of $81 billion at the end of October. However, the run rate reflects recent customer spending rather than revenues earned over a full year.

Both metrics show investors are already paying a substantial premium for Anthropic's expected future growth.

Another concern for investors who buy now is the looming increase in Anthropic’s float — the volume of its shares available for trading. Stakeholders who owned Anthropic shares prior to the IPO are subject to restrictions on selling their shares. But those lock-up periods will expire in a series of tranches from December 2026 through 2027. Each expiration date will allow those early investors to sell a larger fraction of the shares they own. This certainly does not mean these shareholders will sell quickly, but the additional availability of shares to be purchased could put downward pressure on the stock price. Future secondary share issuances could also reduce existing shareholders' ownership stakes in Anthropic.

With all that in mind, I would suggest that you buy Anthropic only if you calculate that its valuation offers sufficient upside potential, despite moderating revenue growth and potential stock dilution.
